extraction.name: DocVQA
extraction.description: A dataset for Visual Question Answering on document images consisting of 50,000 questions defined on 12,000+ document images from various industries and document types including forms, tables, letters, reports, and other business documents.
extraction.creator: Minesh Mathew, Dimosthenis Karatzas, C.V. Jawahar
extraction.citeAs: Minesh Mathew, Dimosthenis Karatzas, C.V. Jawahar. DocVQA: A Dataset for VQA on Document Images. arXiv:2007.00398v3 [cs.CV] 5 Jan 2021
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Questions and answers on selected document images are collected with the help of remote workers using a Web based annotation tool. The annotation process was organized in three stages: (1) workers define up to 10 question-answer pairs per image, (2) verification stage where different workers answer the questions without seeing original answers, and (3) review stage for questions where answers don't match.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Document images sourced from UCSF Industry Documents Library, comprising documents from 5 major industries (tobacco, food, drug, fossil fuel and chemical) spanning from 1900 to 2018. The final set includes pages from 6,071 industry documents.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Documents from as early as 1900 to as recent as 2018, with most documents from the 1960-2000 period
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: OCR tokens are serialized to a single string, separated by space, in top-left to bottom-right order. To approximate answer spans for BERT QA models, the first match of the answer string in the serialized OCR string is found following an approach proposed in TriviaQA.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Documents were downloaded from different collections and pages were hand-picked for use in the dataset. Priority was given to pages with tables, forms, lists and figures over pages with only running text. Binarized images were minimized to avoid poor image quality being a bottleneck.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Three-stage annotation process: Stage 1 - workers define up to 10 question-answer pairs per image with instructions to ask questions answerable using text in the image and enter answers verbatim from the document. Stage 2 - verification by different workers who answer questions and assign question types, with option to flag inappropriate questions. Stage 3 - review by authors for questions where answers don't match between stages.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Questions where answers from stage 1 and stage 2 don't match exactly are sent for review in stage 3. Questions flagged as inappropriate due to language issues or ambiguity are not included in the dataset. Reviewers can edit questions and answers or ignore them.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Multiple ground truth answers per question were encouraged in cases where warranted. Verification stage involved a second annotator answering each question.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Commercial OCR application used for extracting OCR tokens from document images
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset has a higher number of binarized images which affects image quality. The authors tried to minimize binarized images but acknowledge that poor image quality could be a bottleneck for VQA. Most documents are from the 1960-2000 period. There is high representation of food and nutrition related collections as they have a good number of non-binarized images.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Majority of documents in the library are binarized and the binarization has taken a toll on the image quality. Most documents are from the 1960-2000 period. There is large performance gap compared to human performance (94.36% accuracy), with models needing to improve specifically on questions where understanding structure of the document is crucial.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is split into train (39,463 questions on 10,194 images), validation (5,349 questions on 1,286 images), and test (5,188 questions on 1,287 images) splits in an 80-10-10 ratio for training, validation and testing of VQA models on document images.

name.evidence: We present a new dataset for Visual Question Answering (VQA) on document images called DocVQA.

description.evidence: The dataset consists of 50,000 questions defined on 12,000+ document images.

url.evidence: The dataset, code and leaderboard are available at docvqa.org

rai:dataCollection.evidence: Questions and answers on the selected document images are collected with the help of remote workers, using a Web based annotation tool. The annotation process was organized in three stages. In stage 1, workers were shown a document image and asked to define at most 10 question-answer pairs on it... The second annotation stage aims to verify the data collected in the first stage... If none of the answers entered in the first stage match exactly with any of the answers from the second stage, the particular question is sent for review in a third stage.

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: Questions and answers on the selected document images are collected with the help of remote workers, using a Web based annotation tool.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: Images in the dataset are sourced from documents in UCSF Industry Documents Library... The final set of images in the dataset are drawn from pages of 6;071industry documents. We made use of documents from as early as 1900 to as recent as 2018.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: We downloaded documents from different collections and hand picked pages from these documents for use in the dataset... We tried to minimize binarized images in DocVQA since we did not want poor image quality to be a bottleneck for VQA. We also prioritized pages with tables, forms, lists and figures over pages which only have running text.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: In stage 1, workers were shown a document image and asked to define at most 10 question-answer pairs on it. We encouraged the workers to add more than one ground truth answer per question in cases where it is warranted. Workers were instructed to ask questions which can be answered using text present in the image and to enter the answer verbatim from the document... The second annotation stage aims to verify the data collected in the first stage. Here a worker was shown an image and questions defined on it in the first stage (but not the answers from the first stage), and was required to enter answers for the questions. In this stage workers were also required to assign one or more question types to each question... If none of the answers entered in the first stage match exactly with any of the answers from the second stage, the particular question is sent for review in a third stage.

rai:dataAnnotationPlatform.evidence: Questions and answers on the selected document images are collected with the help of remote workers, using a Web based annotation tool.

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: During the second stage, if the worker finds a question inapt owing to language issues or ambiguity, an option to flag the question was provided. Such questions are not included in the dataset. If none of the answers entered in the first stage match exactly with any of the answers from the second stage, the particular question is sent for review in a third stage. Here questions and answers are editable and the reviewer either accepts the question-answer (after editing if necessary) or ignores it.

rai:annotationsPerItem.evidence: We encouraged the workers to add more than one ground truth answer per question in cases where it is warranted... The second annotation stage aims to verify the data collected in the first stage. Here a worker was shown an image and questions defined on it in the first stage (but not the answers from the first stage), and was required to enter answers for the questions.

rai:machineAnnotationTools.evidence: In all our experiments including heuristics and trained baselines, OCR tokens we use are extracted using a commercial OCR application.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: Majority of documents in the library are binarized and the binarization has taken on a toll on the image quality... Most of the documents are from the 1960-2000 period... Although the existing models perform reasonably well on certain types of questions, there is large performance gap compared to human performance (94.36% accuracy). The models need to improve specifically on questions where understanding structure of the document is crucial.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: The data is split randomly in an 80 10 10 ratio to train, validation and test splits. The train split has 39;463questions and 10;194images, the validation split has 5;349questions and 1;286images and the test split has 5;188questions and 1;287images.
